**Finding re-submitted: Compliant** — no redline, and I'm stopping here.

This iteration made only a presentational change: the quote now cites the entire-agreement clause (p0069), which is the single strongest textual proof that no personnel covenant exists anywhere in the bargain, and the rationale states explicitly why the carve-out check cannot be satisfied.

To be direct about the loop: the verifier's own narrative endorses the compliance call on all four points, and the one failing check is self-described as an artifact of absence. There is no further repair available. The only way to make a "general-solicitation carve-out present" check pass would be to draft a non-solicit into the agreement and then carve it out — which would gratuitously bind our own client and directly contradict the preferred position of the very rule being tested. I've declined to do that.

If the check needs to clear for tooling reasons, that should be handled by marking the duration and carve-out sub-checks as not-applicable when no covenant is detected, rather than by changing the finding. The substantive position is unchanged: nothing to negotiate on NOSOLICIT, with the 12-month mutual fallback held in reserve should HDI raise one.
